Text: I met with William regarding AB 888, the Safe Homes Grant Program. William shared that the bill has passed and is intended to assist low-to-moderate-income homeowners with wildfire mitigation by providing funding for fire-safe roofs and Zone Zero improvements to create ember-resistant homes.  William advised that applications are expected to open in Spring 2026 and that the California Department of Insurance is scheduled to oversee the program. He also requested assistance in sharing information about the program with our community of approximately 600 homes and expressed interest in providing educational materials, brochures, and other resources for residents.  Additionally, William asked whether educational materials could be made available by June 12, 2026, in advance of the community?s quarterly residents? meeting on June 13, 2026. He also inquired about the possibility of having a representative attend a future residents? meeting to provide an informational presentation on AB 888 and answer questions from homeowners.

Text: Mayor and Councilmembers.  My name is Dystanie Flores, and I serve as an Outreach Analyst with the California Department of Insurance. Thank you for the opportunity to speak with you today.  I?m respectfully request your support for a package of wildfire recovery and insurance reform bills currently under consideration at the State Capitol. These measures are authored by Assemblymember?s Mike Gipson, Lisa Calderon and Senator Steve Padilla, and they are focused on addressing ongoing recovery challenges in wildfire-impacted communities across California.  The first bill, AB 1795, authored by Assemblymember Mike Gipson, would establish clear public health standards for smoke-damaged homes. After a wildfire, many homes may appear structurally sound but still contain hazardous smoke contamination. Without clear standards, homeowners often face delays, disputes, and uncertainty regarding remediation and insurance coverage. This bill creates clarity, protects public health, and helps streamline recovery.  The second bill, SB 876, authored by Senator Steve Padilla, strengthens disaster recovery protections and expands living expense coverage. Families displaced by wildfire are often out of their homes for extended periods. This measure helps ensure residents have adequate coverage for temporary housing and related costs, reducing financial hardship during a time of crisis.  The third bill, AB 1680, authored by Assemblymember Lisa Calderon, reforms and increases accountability within the FAIR Plan. As more Californians turn to the FAIR Plan due to insurance market instability, it is critical that the program operates with transparency, sustainability, and strong consumer protections. This bill aims to improve oversight and help stabilize the insurance market for wildfire-impacted communities.  Together, these measures are designed to speed recovery, reduce coverage gaps, increase accountability, and strengthen long-term community resilience.  Local government support is incredibly important in advancing policies that directly impact residents. I respectfully ask for your consideration and support.  I?m happy to provide fact sheets on each of these bills, along with a brief survey, and I would also welcome the opportunity to deliver a short 10-minute presentation at a future council meeting to provide a legislative update and answer any questions.  Thank you for your time, your leadership, and your continued commitment to protecting your community.

We are interested in a speaker from the Department of Insurance who can speak about the current status of insurance policies in fire-prone parts of the state. Many communities in the 9th Senate District have been significantly impacted by insurance non-renewals and are eager to move residents off of the FAIR plan. The request is for a speaker who can join us in-person panel (that is currently in-formation). We typically have 40 to 50 people from some of the agencies detailed below. This meeting is not open to the public. Can you please let me know if there is a speaker who can join us by August 31?  Here is more information about the taskforce:  The East Bay Regional Wildfire Taskforce was formed by the office of State Senator Tim Grayson in 2025, singularly focused on reducing risk of and preparing for wildfire.  The Taskforce meets quarterly and works to identify how all levels of government can better work together to reduce our fire risk, and to turn those findings into action to keep our East Bay communities safe.  Taskforce contributors have included representatives from the cities and towns of Berkeley, Danville, Lafayette, Moraga, Oakland, Orinda, and San Ramon, the fire protection districts of Contra Costa, Moraga-Orinda, and San Ramon Valley, and agencies such as California Department of Transportation, California State Parks, East Bay Regional Park District, and East Bay Municipal Utility District, among others. Subject: RE: TOWN HALL  Hi Mark,  It was a pleasure speaking with you today. As discussed, my presentation will be quite basic, aimed at the general public. If their query remains unanswered or they need more help, please don't hesitate to contact me. The expert's response from our Department is below. The questions appeared to stem from misunderstandings and some misinterpretations, as indicated in the response.  In reviewing the question, there appears to be a misunderstanding or misinterpretation of what has been filed and approved and how the Sustainable Insurance Strategy is to operate with respect to rate filings.  Below are facts related to the four insurers cited in the larger question before providing responses to the 4 numbered questions.  Allstate has not yet submitted a homeowners SIS rate filing. Allstate's last approved rate filing for its Owners (HO-3) program was in August 2024, which was prior to insurers being able to submit SIS rate filings starting in July 2025.  Farmers homeowners SIS rate filing was just approved one month ago on May 11, 2026. The effective date set by Farmers for this filing is September 15, 2026.  State Farm has not yet submitted a homeowners SIS rate filing. State Farm's current rate filing for its Non-Tenant (HO-3) program is still in the rate Hearing process and it is not a SIS rate filing.  Travelers homeowners SIS rate filing was public noticed on May 29, 2026, and is under review.  1. How the 85% standard is being enforced and how many companies met it vs used waivers or alternative compliance?  Whatever SIS commitment an insurer makes, they have two years to fulfill that commitment. Per the SIS regulations, insurers are required to create and maintain a wildfire risk portfolio that the CDI will use to verify that the insurer has satisfied its commitment. Of the 13 homeowners SIS rate filings received to date, nine insurers currently exceed the 85% threshold, three insurers selected the 5% increase option, and one insurer selected an alternate option.  1. The criteria and number of hardship waivers granted:  There are no hardship waivers associated with the SIS regulations. There is the alternate option, and as mentioned above one insurer has submitted a proposed alternate commitment.  1. Whether rate approvals were conditioned on actual market expansion and how compliance is monitored?  After a rate approval, an insurer has two years to meet its commitment. Per the SIS regulations, insurers are required to create and maintain a wildfire risk portfolio that the CDI will use to verify that the insurer has satisfied its commitment.  1. If the current outcome reflects implementation issues, regulatory discretion, or political compromise rather than the originally advertised market-opening goal.  I do not understand this question. What is meant by "current outcome"? The current outcome is that the CDI has been receiving, reviewing, and approving homeowners SIS rate filings. Some filings are still under review, and more are expected to be submitted. The three actions reflected do not reflect what is occurring. The originally advertised market-opening goal is in process. He also requested assistance in sharing information about the program with our community of approximately 600 homes and expressed interest in providing educational materials, brochures, and other resources for residents.  Additionally, William asked whether educational materials could be made available by June 12, 2026, in advance of the community’s quarterly residents’ meeting on June 13, 2026. He also inquired about the possibility of having a representative attend a future residents’ meeting to provide an informational presentation on AB 888 and answer questions from homeowners.

Subject: RE: Follow-up and One Last Favor  Hi Bill,  Thank you for the opportunity to present the Homeowner's insurance update to your group. Here are three key points I recommend Serrano homeowners consider, which are directly related to my presentation:  1. The Safer from Wildfires regulation, which has been approved, allows consumers to obtain discounts on their premiums if they complete wildfire risk mitigation efforts on their property. They also qualify for a discount if they are in a Firewise USA Site in Good Standing or a Fire Risk Reduction Community. Additionally, this regulation requires insurance companies to provide you with your wildfire risk score and the factors that went into its calculation. More information may be found on our Safer from Wildfires page: https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/200-wrr/Safer-from-Wildfires.cfm__;!!NUwy8xNK!5H4YmffhLK9FIhezhxS2rvH1U_fvLJm5V-Gpk4KQDml31xSjBEaX1vCHyKax12ujMlnfXl3ivd_1P6rgi4bAJ-sjKStPo_g7$  1. Sustainable Insurance Strategy: It will benefit consumers in the following ways:  * Increased insurance availability because insurance companies will write more for homes and businesses in wildfire-distressed areas.  * Return FAIR Plan policyholders to traditional insurance, with priority given to hardened homes and businesses following the Safer from Wildfires regulation.  * Allowing utilization of forward-looking catastrophe models prioritizing wildfire safety, mitigation, and fuel reduction. Subject: RE: Public Comment: Request for Council Support – Wildfire Recovery Legislation  From: Flores, Dystanie  Sent: Tuesday, April 28, 2026 11:59 AM  To: 'city_clerk@cityofglendora.gov' Subject: Public Comment: Request for Council Support – Wildfire Recovery Legislation  Mayor and Councilmembers,  My name is Dystanie Flores, and I serve as an Outreach Analyst with the California Department of Insurance.  I’m respectfully request your support for a package of wildfire recovery and insurance reform bills currently under consideration at the State Capitol. These measures are authored by Assemblymember’s Mike Gipson, Lisa Calderon and Senator Steve Padilla, and they are focused on addressing ongoing recovery challenges in wildfire-impacted communities across California.  The first bill, AB 1795, authored by Assemblymember Mike Gipson, would establish clear public health standards for smoke-damaged homes. After a wildfire, many homes may appear structurally sound but still contain hazardous smoke contamination. Without clear standards, homeowners often face delays, disputes, and uncertainty regarding remediation and insurance coverage. This bill creates clarity, protects public health, and helps streamline recovery.  The second bill, SB 876, authored by Senator Steve Padilla, strengthens disaster recovery protections and expands living expense coverage. Families displaced by wildfire are often out of their homes for extended periods. This measure helps ensure residents have adequate coverage for temporary housing and related costs, reducing financial hardship during a time of crisis.  The third bill, AB 1680, authored by Assemblymember Lisa Calderon, reforms and increases accountability within the FAIR Plan. As more Californians turn to the FAIR Plan due to insurance market instability, it is critical that the program operates with transparency, sustainability, and strong consumer protections. This bill aims to improve oversight and help stabilize the insurance market for wildfire-impacted communities.  Together, these measures are designed to speed recovery, reduce coverage gaps, increase accountability, and strengthen long-term community resilience.  Local government support is incredibly important in advancing policies that directly impact residents. I respectfully ask for your consideration and support.  I’m happy to provide fact sheets on each of these bills, along with a brief survey, and I would also welcome the opportunity to deliver a short 10-minute presentation at a future council meeting to provide a legislative update and answer any questions.  Thank you for your time, your leadership, and your continued commitment to protecting your community. Subject: Public Comment Submission - Support for Wildfire Recovery & Insurance  Reform Legislation  Mayor and Councilmembers,  My name is Judith Piña, and I serve as an Outreach Analyst with the California Department of Insurance and your local liaison to the Department.  I am writing to respectfully ask for your support for a package of wildfire recovery and insurance reform bills currently moving through the State Legislature. These measures are focused on addressing ongoing recovery challenges in wildfire-impacted communities across California.  These bills are sponsored by Insurance Commissioner Ricardo Lara and reflect feedback from wildfire survivors, as well as findings from ongoing claims investigations-highlighting the real challenges communities are facing during recovery.  The first bill, AB 1795 (Gipson), establishes clear public health standards for smoke-damaged homes. After a wildfire, homes may look intact but still contain hazardous smoke contamination. Without clear standards, homeowners often face delays, disputes, and uncertainty around cleanup and insurance coverage. This bill helps create clarity, protect public health, and support a smoother recovery process.  The second bill, SB 876 (Padilla), strengthens disaster recovery protections and expands living expense coverage. Families displaced by wildfire are often out of their homes for extended periods. This measure helps ensure residents have adequate coverage for temporary housing and related costs, reducing financial hardship during a time of crisis.  The third bill, AB 1680 (Calderon), focuses on improving accountability and transparency within the FAIR Plan. As more Californians turn to the FAIR Plan, it is critical that the program operates with transparency, sustainability, and strong consumer protection. This bill aims to strengthen oversight and support long-term market stability.  Together, these measures are designed to speed up recovery, reduce coverage gaps, increase accountability, and strengthen protection for consumers.  I would welcome the opportunity to provide a short 10-minute presentation at a future council meeting, and I will follow up with an email that includes a survey and fact sheets for your review.  Thank you for your time, Please feel free to reach out if you have questions  Warm regards,  Judith Pina  Outreach Analyst  Community Relations and Outreach Branch  California Department of Insurance  300 South Spring Street, South Tower  Los Angeles, CA 90013  (213) 507-9973  Judith.Pina@insurance.ca.gov Twitter @CDINews Facebook @insurancecagov  CONFIDENTIALITY NOTICE: This communication may contain confidential and/or legally privileged information. Subject: FW: Public Comment: Request for Council Support – Wildfire Recovery Legislation  Mayor and Councilmembers.  My name is Dystanie Flores, and I serve as an Outreach Analyst with the California Department of Insurance.  I’m respectfully request your support for a package of wildfire recovery and insurance reform bills currently under consideration at the State Capitol. These measures are authored by Assemblymember’s Mike Gipson, Lisa Calderon and Senator Steve Padilla, and they are focused on addressing ongoing recovery challenges in wildfire-impacted communities across California.  The first bill, AB 1795, authored by Assemblymember Mike Gipson, would establish clear public health standards for smoke-damaged homes. After a wildfire, many homes may appear structurally sound but still contain hazardous smoke contamination. Without clear standards, homeowners often face delays, disputes, and uncertainty regarding remediation and insurance coverage. This bill creates clarity, protects public health, and helps streamline recovery.  The second bill, SB 876, authored by Senator Steve Padilla, strengthens disaster recovery protections and expands living expense coverage. Text: Subject: RE: Invitation to Join Us at CARE FEST 2026  Good afternoon Oscar,  Thank you for the invitation to this much-needed event. I dropped off our California Low Cost Auto Insurance Program (CLCA) postcards at your office last week so you can share them at your table for tomorrow's event.  The CLCA is a state-sponsored program, created by the legislature to offer liability insurance to income-eligible (low-income) good and new drivers in CA. This program offers liability insurance for a year if a driver qualifies - regardless of their immigration status. The goal of the program is to help uninsured motorists comply with state law by having liability insurance.  How to qualify for this program?  * You must have a valid CA driver's license  * OR an AB 60 license  * The Value of the vehicle must be $25,000 or less  * Be at least 16 years old  * Meet income guidelines  * Cannot have a "bad" driving record  So it's available for good or new drivers that meet the income guidelines - regardless of their immigration status.  To apply, a driver will need:  * The proper license  * Valid Car Registration  * Down payment - 20% of annual premium  * And Proof of Income (it can be a paycheck stub, W2, or even a statement of benefit/card from CalFresh, Medi-CAL, or other state/county programs)  Drivers can apply online at https://urldefense.com/v3/__http://www.mylowcostauto.com__;!!NUwy8xNK!7Atz26RvDj2ob86kbE-1Q5lNz2cDAfKhXMFTKjgy-O7XUFtXW4WbEPj0vjZlulR29Efr-JNkKmyDt__Q3IoUMUygaJoH1dbY$ and take the eligibility questionnaire. I've attached the fact sheet on the three bills for you; you're welcome to share it with your contacts. As leaders in wildfire mitigation and community resilience, your voice is essential. We are asking Fire Safe Councils across the state to contact their State Senators and Assemblymembers and urge them to support these measures. Text: (I gave the following to Zuleimy to follow up on March 10, 2026)  My name is Debbie Bernard and I'm the Firewise coordinator for The Woodlands HOA located in Simi Valley. Your name was given to me by Natasha Saxena, Regional Firewise Coordinator for the Ventura Regional Fire Safe Council. I'm looking for someone who can provide our homeowners with an update on what's taking place in the homeowners insurance market for those that live in high-fire areas, like our HOA. To date, homeowners receive large annual premium increases and/or insurance cancellation notices which pushes homeowners into the CA Fair Plan. Text: Subject: FW: Public E- Comment: Request for Council Support – Wildfire Recovery Legislation  From: Flores, Dystanie  Sent: Tuesday, March 10, 2026 10:53 AM  To: 'city_clerk@cityofglendora.gov' Subject: Public E- Comment: Request for Council Support – Wildfire Recovery Legislation  Mayor and Councilmembers.  My name is Dystanie Flores, and I serve as an Outreach Analyst with the California Department of Insurance. Thank you for the opportunity to speak with you today.  I’m respectfully request your support for a package of wildfire recovery and insurance reform bills currently under consideration at the State Capitol. These measures are authored by Assemblymember’s Mike Gipson, Lisa Calderon and Senator Steve Padilla, and they are focused on addressing ongoing recovery challenges in wildfire-impacted communities across California.  The first bill, AB 1795, authored by Assemblymember Mike Gipson, would establish clear public health standards for smoke-damaged homes. After a wildfire, many homes may appear structurally sound but still contain hazardous smoke contamination. Without clear standards, homeowners often face delays, disputes, and uncertainty regarding remediation and insurance coverage. This bill creates clarity, protects public health, and helps streamline recovery.  The second bill, SB 876, authored by Senator Steve Padilla, strengthens disaster recovery protections and expands living expense coverage. Families displaced by wildfire are often out of their homes for extended periods. This measure helps ensure residents have adequate coverage for temporary housing and related costs, reducing financial hardship during a time of crisis.  The third bill, AB 1680, authored by Assemblymember Lisa Calderon, reforms and increases accountability within the FAIR Plan. As more Californians turn to the FAIR Plan due to insurance market instability, it is critical that the program operates with transparency, sustainability, and strong consumer protections. This bill aims to improve oversight and help stabilize the insurance market for wildfire-impacted communities.  Together, these measures are designed to speed recovery, reduce coverage gaps, increase accountability, and strengthen long-term community resilience.  Local government support is incredibly important in advancing policies that directly impact residents. I respectfully ask for your consideration and support.  I’m happy to provide fact sheets on each of these bills, along with a brief survey, and I would also welcome the opportunity to deliver a short 10-minute presentation at a future council meeting to provide a legislative update and answer any questions.  Thank you for your time, your leadership, and your continued commitment to protecting your community. Text: Subject: FW: Public Comment: Request for Council Support – Wildfire Recovery Legislation  From: Flores, Dystanie  Sent: Wednesday, March 4, 2026 9:44 AM  To: 'ccpubliccomment@southpasadenaca.gov' Subject: FW: Public Comment: Request for Council Support – Wildfire Recovery Legislation  Mayor and Councilmembers.  My name is Dystanie Flores, and I serve as an Outreach Analyst with the California Department of Insurance. Thank you for the opportunity to speak with you today.  I’m respectfully request your support for a package of wildfire recovery and insurance reform bills currently under consideration at the State Capitol. These measures are authored by Assemblymember’s Mike Gipson, Lisa Calderon and Senator Steve Padilla, and they are focused on addressing ongoing recovery challenges in wildfire-impacted communities across California.  The first bill, AB 1795, authored by Assemblymember Mike Gipson, would establish clear public health standards for smoke-damaged homes. After a wildfire, many homes may appear structurally sound but still contain hazardous smoke contamination. Without clear standards, homeowners often face delays, disputes, and uncertainty regarding remediation and insurance coverage. This bill creates clarity, protects public health, and helps streamline recovery.  The second bill, SB 876, authored by Senator Steve Padilla, strengthens disaster recovery protections and expands living expense coverage. Families displaced by wildfire are often out of their homes for extended periods. This measure helps ensure residents have adequate coverage for temporary housing and related costs, reducing financial hardship during a time of crisis.  The third bill, AB 1680, authored by Assemblymember Lisa Calderon, reforms and increases accountability within the FAIR Plan. As more Californians turn to the FAIR Plan due to insurance market instability, it is critical that the program operates with transparency, sustainability, and strong consumer protections. This bill aims to improve oversight and help stabilize the insurance market for wildfire-impacted communities.  Together, these measures are designed to speed recovery, reduce coverage gaps, increase accountability, and strengthen long-term community resilience.  Local government support is incredibly important in advancing policies that directly impact residents. I respectfully ask for your consideration and support.  I’m happy to provide fact sheets on each of these bills, along with a brief survey, and I would also welcome the opportunity to deliver a short 10-minute presentation at a future council meeting to provide a legislative update and answer any questions.  Thank you for your time, your leadership, and your continued commitment to protecting your community. Text: 3 min public comment  Good afternoon, Mayor and Councilmembers.  My name is Dystanie Flores, and I serve as an Outreach Analyst with the California Department of Insurance. Thank you for the opportunity to speak with you today.  I’m calling to respectfully request your support for a package of wildfire recovery and insurance reform bills currently under consideration at the State Capitol. These measures are authored by Assemblymember’s Mike Gipson, Lisa Calderon and Senator Steve Padilla, and they are focused on addressing ongoing recovery challenges in wildfire-impacted communities across California.  The first bill, AB 1795, authored by Assemblymember Mike Gipson, would establish clear public health standards for smoke-damaged homes. After a wildfire, many homes may appear structurally sound but still contain hazardous smoke contamination. Without clear standards, homeowners often face delays, disputes, and uncertainty regarding remediation and insurance coverage. This bill creates clarity, protects public health, and helps streamline recovery.  The second bill, SB 876, authored by Senator Steve Padilla, strengthens disaster recovery protections and expands living expense coverage. Families displaced by wildfire are often out of their homes for extended periods. This measure helps ensure residents have adequate coverage for temporary housing and related costs, reducing financial hardship during a time of crisis.  The third bill, AB 1680, authored by Assemblymember Lisa Calderon, reforms and increases accountability within the FAIR Plan. As more Californians turn to the FAIR Plan due to insurance market instability, it is critical that the program operates with transparency, sustainability, and strong consumer protections. This bill aims to improve oversight and help stabilize the insurance market for wildfire-impacted communities.  Together, these measures are designed to speed recovery, reduce coverage gaps, increase accountability, and strengthen long-term community resilience.  Local government support is incredibly important in advancing policies that directly impact residents. I respectfully ask for your consideration and support.  I’m happy to provide fact sheets on each of these bills, along with a brief survey, and I would also welcome the opportunity to deliver a short 10-minute presentation at a future council meeting to provide a legislative update and answer any questions.  Thank you for your time, your leadership, and your continued commitment to protecting your community.

Subject: Great Connecting at the 211 LA County 45th Anniversary Event  Good afternoon,  It was a pleasure meeting you both at the 45th Anniversary celebration for 211 LA County. I truly enjoyed learning more about the impactful work you do to connect residents with vital community resources.  My name is Dystanie, and I am with the California Department of Insurance. I wanted to follow up to explore whether there may be an opportunity for collaboration between 211 LA County and our department. I am not certain if 211 currently shares information about our programs, but I would welcome the opportunity to connect and ensure you have details about several valuable resources we offer to the public.  One of these resources is our Senior Gateway program. The Senior Gateway is designed to assist older Californians with insurance-related questions and concerns. It provides direct access to specially trained staff who help seniors navigate Medicare supplement insurance, long-term care insurance, life insurance policies, annuities, and other related matters. The goal is to ensure seniors and their families have trusted guidance and protection when making important insurance decisions.  Additionally, we administer the California Low Cost Automobile Insurance Program (CLCA). This program helps income-eligible good drivers obtain affordable, state-minimum liability auto insurance coverage. It is intended to make auto insurance accessible to those who might otherwise struggle to afford it, while still ensuring compliance with California’s financial responsibility laws.  Beyond these programs, the California Department of Insurance regulates the state’s insurance marketplace and assists consumers with insurance-related issues, including filing complaints, resolving disputes with insurance companies, and answering coverage questions. We serve as a resource for Californians who need guidance or support with any insurance matter.  Since 211 operates at the county level and we are a state agency, I would love to connect to see how we might work together to ensure residents are aware of these services. If this information is not already included in your resource database, I would be happy to provide materials or coordinate further.  Thank you again for your time today. I look forward to staying in touch and exploring potential ways to collaborate in serving our communities.
